# 12-Week Post-Cardiac Rehab Fitness Programme

**Client Profile:** 58-year-old male, 6 months post-MI, cleared for moderate intensity only.

## Key Safety Parameters
- **HR cap:** 115 bpm (use chest strap monitor every session)
- **RPE target:** 11–13 on Borg 6–20 scale (light to somewhat hard)
- **No Valsalva:** exhale on every exertion, no breath-holding
- **No max lifts:** RIR 3–4 minimum, never grind reps
- **Warning signs to halt session:** chest pain, dizziness, dyspnoea disproportionate to effort, palpitations, unusual fatigue. Ensure he carries GTN spray if prescribed.
- **Warm-up:** 8–10 min cycle ergometer at 60–80W, gradual ramp
- **Cool-down:** 5–10 min walking + breathing drills + mobility
- **Frequency:** 4 sessions/week (2 resistance, 2 cardio-focused). Rest days walked, not sedentary.

---

## PHASE 1: FOUNDATION (Weeks 1–4)
**Goal:** Re-establish movement patterns, build aerobic base, build confidence with loaded work. Machine-based resistance to control range and remove stabiliser fatigue.

### Resistance Sessions A & B (2x/week, full body)

**Session A**
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Leg press (machine) | 2 x 12 | Light load, full exhale on press |
| Chest press (machine) | 2 x 12 | Neutral grip if available |
| Seated row (machine) | 2 x 12 | Pause at chest, controlled return |
| Lat pulldown | 2 x 12 | Wide neutral grip |
| Standing calf raise (machine) | 2 x 15 | |
| Dead bug | 2 x 8/side | Core, no breath holding |

**Session B**
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat to box | 2 x 10 | Light KB, controlled tempo |
| DB bench press (flat) | 2 x 12 | Light DBs |
| Cable row (single arm) | 2 x 12/side | |
| DB shoulder press (seated, supported) | 2 x 10 | Keep elbows in front |
| Pallof press (cable) | 2 x 10/side | |
| Bird dog | 2 x 8/side | |

**Loading guide W1–4:** RPE 11–12, RIR 4. Increase load only when all reps feel effortless.

### Cardio Sessions C & D (2x/week)
- **Session C:** 20 min continuous cycle ergometer, HR 95–105 bpm (~60% APMHR)
- **Session D:** 20 min treadmill walk at 4–5% incline, HR 95–110 bpm

Add 2 min per week to cardio duration. By week 4: 28 min steady-state.

---

## PHASE 2: PROGRESSION (Weeks 5–8)
**Goal:** Introduce free-weight patterns, increase volume modestly, introduce light interval work within HR cap.

### Resistance Sessions A & B (2x/week)

**Session A**
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| DB goblet squat | 3 x 10 | |
| DB incline press | 3 x 10 | |
| Chest-supported row | 3 x 10 | |
| Lat pulldown | 3 x 10 | |
| Split squat (rear foot on floor, hand support) | 2 x 8/leg | |
| DB farmer's carry | 2 x 30 m | Light, nasal breathing |
| Side plank | 2 x 20 sec/side | |

**Session B**
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trap bar deadlift (high handles) | 3 x 8 | Light, focus on hip hinge and exhale on lift |
| Seated DB shoulder press | 3 x 10 | |
| Cable row | 3 x 10 | |
| DB Romanian deadlift | 2 x 10 | |
| Cable triceps + DB curl superset | 2 x 12 each | |
| Cable woodchop (mid) | 2 x 10/side | |

**Loading guide W5–8:** RPE 12–13, RIR 3. Add 2.5kg or 1 rep per week as tolerated.

### Cardio Sessions C & D (2x/week)
- **Session C (steady):** 30 min cycle, HR 100–110 bpm
- **Session D (intervals):** 6 x (2 min brisk walk @ HR 110–115 / 2 min easy walk @ HR 90–95). Total 24 min + warm-up/cool-down. Progress to 7, then 8 rounds across weeks 5–8.

---

## PHASE 3: CONSOLIDATION (Weeks 9–12)
**Goal:** Build resilience, increase work capacity, maintain conservative intensity. Prepare for transition to independent training or higher rehab phase pending GP review.

### Resistance Sessions A & B (2x/week)

**Session A — Lower bias**
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trap bar deadlift | 3 x 8 | RPE 13 max |
| Goblet squat | 3 x 10 | |
| DB walking lunge | 2 x 8/leg | |
| Leg curl machine | 3 x 12 | |
| DB bench press | 3 x 10 | |
| Cable row | 3 x 10 | |
| Hanging knee raise (or dead bug) | 2 x 10 | |

**Session B — Upper bias**
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Landmine press | 3 x 8/side | Safer overhead alternative |
| Chest-supported DB row | 3 x 10 | |
| Incline DB press | 3 x 10 | |
| Lat pulldown | 3 x 10 | |
| Leg press | 3 x 12 | |
| Suitcase carry | 2 x 30 m/side | |
| Pallof press | 2 x 12/side | |

**Loading guide W9–12:** RPE 12–13, RIR 3. Final week (12): deload — reduce sets by 1, drop RPE to 11.

### Cardio Sessions C & D (2x/week)
- **Session C:** 35–40 min cycle or incline walk, HR 105–115 bpm
- **Session D (intervals):** 8–10 x (2 min @ HR 110–115 / 2 min @ HR 90–95). By week 11, trial 3 min work / 2 min recovery x 6 if tolerating well.

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Integration
- **Sleep:** target 7–8 hours; flag any new sleep apnoea symptoms to GP.
- **Daily steps:** build from 5,000 to 8,000 across 12 weeks.
- **Stretching/mobility:** 10 min on rest days — thoracic spine, hips, calves.
- **Hydration:** 30–35 ml/kg/day; more on training days.
- **Stress:** introduce 5 min diaphragmatic breathing post-session — helps vagal tone and counters Valsalva habits.

## Monitoring Protocol
- Resting HR and BP logged weekly (morning).
- Session RPE and HR peak logged each session.
- Re-check with cardiologist at week 6 and week 12 before any progression beyond moderate intensity.
- Halt and refer if: rising resting HR trend, new arrhythmia awareness, exertional symptoms, or BP >160/100 pre-session.

## Progression Out of Programme
At week 12, if asymptomatic and cardiologist approves, consider Phase IV cardiac rehab progression: introduce slightly heavier loading (RPE 14, RIR 2), longer intervals, and gradual HR cap increase to 75% APMHR (~122 bpm). Do not progress unilaterally without medical clearance.

# Nutrition Plan — Cardiac Health Focus

**Client context:** 58yo male, 6 months post-MI, training 4x/week at moderate intensity. Assumed on standard post-MI medication (statin, beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor, antiplatelet — confirm with client/GP). Plan assumes no diabetes, CKD, or warfarin use — flag these if present as they change the prescription.

## Core Framework: Mediterranean Pattern
The strongest evidence base for secondary cardiac prevention (PREDIMED, Lyon Heart Study). This is the foundation — not a "diet" but a long-term eating pattern he can sustain.

---

## Daily Targets

### Energy
Estimate maintenance at **~2,200–2,500 kcal/day** (assumes ~80–90 kg, moderately active). Adjust based on 4-week weight trend:
- Weight loss goal (if BMI >25): 300–400 kcal deficit
- Weight stable goal: match intake to output
- Reassess monthly with waist circumference (target <94 cm) more than scale weight

### Macronutrients
| Macro | Target | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 1.4–1.6 g/kg (~120–140 g) | Preserve lean mass during training; supports recovery |
| Carbohydrate | 45–50% of calories | Mostly low-GI, fibre-rich |
| Fat | 30–35% of calories | Heavily weighted toward mono- and polyunsaturated |
| Saturated fat | <7% of calories (~17 g) | Post-MI secondary prevention target |
| Fibre | 30–35 g/day | LDL reduction, glycaemic control |

### Key Micronutrients & Compounds
- **Sodium:** <2,000 mg/day (strict — most will come from hidden sources)
- **Potassium:** 3,500–4,700 mg/day (caution if on ACE/ARB + spironolactone — check bloods)
- **Omega-3 (EPA+DHA):** 1–2 g/day from oily fish 2–3x/week
- **Added sugar:** <25 g/day
- **Alcohol:** ideally zero; if drinking, ≤7 units/week, never >2 in a session

---

## Food List

### Eat Freely
- **Vegetables:** all non-starchy — leafy greens, tomatoes, peppers, courgette, aubergine, broccoli, cauliflower, onions, garlic. Target 5+ portions/day.
- **Fruits:** berries, apples, pears, citrus, stone fruit. 2–3 portions/day.
- **Legumes:** lentils, chickpeas, black beans, kidney beans. 4+ servings/week.
- **Whole grains:** oats, barley, brown rice, quinoa, wholegrain sourdough, bulgur.
- **Nuts & seeds:** 30 g/day — walnuts (omega-3), almonds, flaxseed, chia. Unsalted only.
- **Olive oil:** extra virgin, primary cooking and dressing fat. 3–4 tbsp/day.
- **Oily fish:** salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring, trout. 2–3 servings/week.
- **White fish & seafood:** unlimited.
- **Poultry:** skinless chicken/turkey, 2–3 servings/week.
- **Eggs:** up to 6/week.
- **Low-fat dairy or fortified alternatives:** Greek yoghurt, kefir, skyr. 1–2 servings/day.
- **Herbs & spices:** unlimited — replace salt with garlic, lemon, herbs, chilli, pepper.

### Limit
- **Red meat:** ≤1 serving/week (lean cuts only)
- **Cheese:** small amounts of feta, parmesan, cottage cheese
- **Refined grains:** white bread, white pasta, white rice — occasional
- **Butter:** small amounts; use olive oil instead

### Avoid
- Processed meats (bacon, sausage, ham, salami) — strongest dietary risk factor for CHD recurrence
- Deep-fried foods and anything cooked in palm/coconut oil at restaurants
- Trans fats — check labels for "partially hydrogenated"
- Sugary drinks, fruit juice (>150 ml/day), confectionery
- Ready meals, instant soups, stock cubes (sodium bombs)
- Pastries, biscuits, commercial baked goods

---

## Sample Daily Structure (~2,300 kcal)

**Breakfast (~500 kcal)**
- 60 g oats cooked with semi-skimmed milk or unsweetened soy milk
- 1 tbsp ground flaxseed, handful of berries, 20 g walnuts
- Black coffee or green tea

**Mid-morning (~200 kcal)**
- Greek yoghurt (150 g, 0–2% fat) with 1 tsp honey and an apple

**Lunch (~600 kcal)**
- Large salad: mixed leaves, tomato, cucumber, red onion, 80 g tinned salmon or sardines, half a tin of chickpeas, 1/2 avocado
- Dressing: 1.5 tbsp olive oil + lemon + herbs
- 1 slice wholegrain sourdough

**Pre-training snack (if afternoon session) (~200 kcal)**
- Banana + small handful of almonds
- Eaten 60–90 min pre-session

**Dinner (~700 kcal)**
- 150 g grilled chicken breast, baked white fish, or lentil stew
- Large portion roasted vegetables in olive oil
- 60 g (dry weight) quinoa, brown rice, or bulgur
- Side salad

**Evening (~100 kcal, optional)**
- Square of 85% dark chocolate, herbal tea
- Or cottage cheese with cinnamon

---

## Training-Day Nutrition

**Pre-session (60–90 min before):**
Light carb + small protein — banana with yoghurt, oatcakes with hummus, slice of toast with eggs. Avoid heavy/fatty meals close to training.

**Intra-session:**
Water only — no need for sports drinks at this intensity.

**Post-session (within 60 min):**
~25–30 g protein + carbs. Examples: Greek yoghurt with berries and granola; chicken and rice bowl; lentil soup with bread; whey shake with a banana if convenient.

**Hydration:**
2.5–3 L water/day. More on training days. Watch for diuretic interaction if on bumetanide/furosemide — flag with GP.

---

## Practical Implementation Strategy

### Weeks 1–4: Foundations
- Audit current intake with 3-day food diary
- Eliminate processed meats and sugary drinks first — biggest single wins
- Switch cooking fat to extra virgin olive oil
- Aim for 5 vegetable portions/day
- Read sodium labels — anything >1.5 g salt per 100 g is high

### Weeks 5–8: Build
- Introduce 2 oily fish meals/week
- Add legumes to 4 meals/week
- Establish breakfast template (oats-based)
- Daily 30 g nut portion habit
- Caffeine cap: 3 cups coffee/day, none after 2pm

### Weeks 9–12: Refine
- Dial in protein distribution: 30 g/meal across 4 meals
- Standardise pre/post-training nutrition around session timing
- Review weight, waist, BP trends — adjust calories if needed
- Plan for sustainability beyond 12 weeks — restaurants, holidays, social meals

---

## Supplements

**Recommended (with GP sign-off):**
- **Vitamin D3:** 1,000–2,000 IU/day, October–March (UK default)
- **Omega-3:** only if not hitting 2 oily fish portions/week — 1 g EPA+DHA combined. Caution if on antiplatelets — discuss with GP first.

**Not recommended:**
- High-dose antioxidants (vit E, beta-carotene) — no benefit, possible harm post-MI
- Red yeast rice — interacts with statins
- Pre-workouts with stimulants — caffeine + yohimbine + synephrine combinations are contraindicated
- Creatine is *probably* fine but discuss with cardiologist first given the case

---

## Monitoring

Track monthly:
- Weight and waist circumference
- Resting BP (home monitor, morning)
- Subjective energy and training recovery

Recommend GP review at week 12 for:
- Lipid panel (target LDL <1.4 mmol/L post-MI per current guidance)
- HbA1c
- U&Es (especially if increasing potassium-rich foods)

---

## Red Flags to Refer

- Unintended weight loss >2 kg/month
- New oedema or shortness of breath (could indicate fluid balance issue with sodium changes)
- Persistent GI symptoms with fibre increase — titrate up more slowly
- Any interaction concerns with anticoagulants and dietary vitamin K (leafy greens) — relevant if on warfarin, not DOACs

## The Evidence on HIIT Post-MI

HIIT in cardiac populations is actually **well-studied and increasingly endorsed** — but with significant caveats. The main trials (SAINTEX-CAD, SMARTEX-HF, and meta-analyses by Hannan et al.) show:

**The good:**
- HIIT produces **greater VO2max improvements** than moderate continuous training in stable cardiac patients
- Better improvements in endothelial function and left ventricular remodelling
- Comparable safety profile to MICT **in supervised, screened populations**
- Effective for weight management and metabolic markers

**The caveats — and they're important:**
- Nearly all positive trials used patients who were **>3–6 months post-event, on stable medication, and had completed formal cardiac rehab**
- Patients were **screened with CPET or stress echo** before HIIT prescription
- Sessions were **supervised by clinical exercise physiologists**, often with telemetry
- Most protocols used **4x4 (Norwegian) intervals**, not the CrossFit-style HIIT the general public means by the term
- **Exclusions matter:** uncontrolled arrhythmia, recent revascularisation (<4 weeks), unstable angina, severe LV dysfunction, exercise-induced ischaemia all disqualify

---

## What This Means For Your Client

He could be a candidate — but only if:

1. **>12 months post-MI** by the time HIIT is introduced (so realistically not until ~6 months after this programme ends)
2. **Completed full cardiac rehab** including Phase IV
3. **Cardiologist formally clears him for vigorous intensity**
4. **Recent CPET or stress test** confirming no exercise-induced ischaemia and identifying his ischaemic threshold
5. **Stable on medication** with no recent dose changes
6. **No arrhythmias** on monitoring
7. **Demonstrated tolerance** of moderate-vigorous intensity (75–85% APMHR) for at least 4–6 weeks first

That's not gatekeeping — that's the inclusion criteria from the actual trials. You can't extrapolate trial outcomes to a patient who wouldn't have been allowed in the trial.

## What "HIIT for Cardiac Patients" Actually Looks Like

When the time comes, this is the protocol with the strongest evidence base — **not** burpees and box jumps.

### Norwegian 4x4 Protocol
- 10 min warm-up at 60–70% APMHR
- 4 x (4 min at 85–95% APMHR / 3 min active recovery at 60–70% APMHR)
- 5 min cool-down
- Total: ~40 min
- Frequency: 2x/week maximum, never on consecutive days
- Modality: cycle ergometer or treadmill (no impact, controlled environment, easy to stop)

**Key features:**
- Long intervals (4 min), not short sprints — this is the critical safety point
- Submaximal — never to volitional exhaustion
- HR-targeted, not effort-targeted
- Always supervised in early sessions
- Chest strap HR monitoring mandatory

### What it is NOT
- ❌ Tabata (20s/10s) — too short, BP spikes too high
- ❌ Sprint intervals — too intense, ischaemic risk
- ❌ Circuit-style "HIIT" classes — uncontrolled HR, often involves Valsalva
- ❌ Anything to failure or "max effort"
- ❌ Heavy weights done fast — combines worst of both

If he says "I want to do HIIT" and he's picturing what he sees on Instagram, that's not what we'd ever prescribe. Worth clarifying that conversation early.

## The Cardiac-Specific Problem With Heavy Compounds

Barbell back squats and conventional deadlifts are excellent exercises — but they have two features that conflict with his clearance:

1. **Valsalva manoeuvre is nearly reflexive** under a loaded bar. Even trained lifters Valsalva on heavy sets without realising. Intra-thoracic pressure spikes BP dramatically — systolic readings of 300+ mmHg have been recorded during heavy squats. That's the opposite of what we want post-MI.

2. **Spinal loading at near-max effort** is where the BP spike is highest. We're already RIR 3 capped, which helps — but the bar on the back still loads the system differently than the alternatives.

This doesn't mean "never." It means **right variation, right load, right cueing, right phase.**

---

## What I'd Add and What I'd Avoid

### ✅ Add these
- **Barbell back squat (high-bar, moderate load)** — controlled, RIR 3–4, strict breathing
- **Barbell front squat** — actually safer than back squat in this context. Self-limiting load (you drop it before you Valsalva), more upright torso, less spinal compression
- **Romanian deadlift (barbell)** — hinge pattern, doesn't start from the floor, controlled eccentric
- **Continue trap bar deadlift** as the primary "deadlift" — already in the programme and ideal

### ⚠️ Use cautiously
- **Conventional barbell deadlift from floor** — only in Phase 3, light loads, perfect technique. The start position requires the most intra-abdominal pressure
- **Overhead barbell press** — BP spike from overhead loading. Landmine press is the safer substitute

### ❌ Avoid in this block
- Barbell squat or deadlift at RPE >13
- Anything resembling 1–5 rep maxes
- Touch-and-go deadlifts (encourages breath holding across reps)
- Sumo deadlift at depth — hip position encourages Valsalva
- Olympic lifts and derivatives (cleans, snatches) — explosive and high BP
- Heavy good mornings — high spinal load, high BP

## The Cueing Non-Negotiables

These matter more than the exercise selection. Drill these from day one:

1. **"Exhale on exertion"** — every single rep, every single set. Hiss through pursed lips on the way up. If he can't talk through a rep, the load is too heavy or he's holding his breath.
2. **No belt** — belts encourage Valsalva and intra-abdominal pressure. He doesn't need one at the loads we're using.
3. **RIR 3 minimum** — if rep 8 of 10 feels grindy, rack it. Leaving reps in the tank is the rule, not the exception.
4. **No PR attempts, ever, in this block.** Frame every session as practice, not testing.
5. **Reset between reps on deadlifts** — full breath out at the bottom, fresh breath before next rep. No bounced reps.

If he can't follow these cues, he doesn't get the barbell. That's the deal.

## Technique Coaching Priorities

For **back squat**, watch for:
- Breath holding (the biggest risk) — make him verbalise the exhale audibly
- Excessive forward lean — indicates ankle mobility issues, may need elevated heels
- Bar position — high bar is more upright, easier on lower back
- Depth — to parallel only, no need for ATG. Reduces BP spike vs. deep squat
- Knees tracking over toes

For **Romanian deadlift**, watch for:
- Soft knee bend (not a squat)
- Hinge from hips, neutral spine
- Bar travels close to legs
- Stop when hamstrings limit — usually mid-shin
- Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down

For **conventional deadlift** (Phase 3 only), watch for:
- Set-up position — shoulders slightly ahead of bar, hips between knees and shoulders
- **Full exhale before initiating the lift** — counterintuitive but critical for him
- Bar against shins, travels in straight line
- Lockout without hyperextension
- **Reset on the floor every rep** — no bounce, full breath cycle between reps
- If he's grinding, the set is over

| Post-set HR recovery | Should drop to <100 within 90 seconds. If not, reduce next set load |
| Subjective feeling | Any dizziness, head pressure, or "head feels weird" — done for the day |

Some days he won't be in shape for heavy compound work, and you need to call it. Skip barbell variations and substitute machine/DB work if:

- Resting HR >10 bpm above his normal baseline
- BP >145/90 pre-session
- Slept <6 hours
- Reports any chest/cardiac symptoms in the past 48 hours
- Medication changes in the last 7 days
- Feeling unusually fatigued or unwell

If he has **any history of aortic involvement** — aortic aneurysm, aortic dissection, significant aortic stenosis, or Marfan/connective tissue concerns — **barbell back squats and deadlifts come off the table entirely.** The BP spike risk is too high regardless of cueing. # 12-Week Post-MI Strength & Conditioning Programme — Full Integrated Version

**Client:** 58-year-old male, 6 months post-MI, cardiac rehab cleared for moderate intensity only.

---

## Safety Parameters (Apply to Every Session)

- **HR cap:** 115 bpm (~70% APMHR). Chest strap monitor required every session.
- **RPE cap:** 13/20 (somewhat hard). Most work at 11–12.
- **RIR:** Minimum 3 reps in reserve on every set.
- **Valsalva:** Strictly forbidden. Audible exhale on every exertion. Silent rep = rack it.
- **No belts.** No max attempts. No grinding reps.
- **Pre-session checks:** Resting HR, BP if available, subjective wellbeing. Cancel barbell work if BP >145/90, RHR >10 bpm above baseline, slept <6 hours, or any cardiac symptoms in past 48 hours.
- **Stop criteria:** Chest pain/pressure, dizziness, disproportionate breathlessness, palpitations, head pressure, anything that feels wrong. Stop immediately, sit, monitor, call medical help if symptoms persist.
- **Aortic check:** Before introducing barbell work in Phase 2, confirm with cardiologist/discharge summary that there is no aortic aneurysm, dissection history, severe aortic stenosis, or connective tissue disorder. If any of these are present, barbell back squat and conventional deadlift come off the programme permanently — substitute trap bar, front squat, and DB/machine variations only.

---

## Weekly Structure

| Day | Session | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | Lower body strength | Resistance |
| Tuesday | Cardio | Aerobic |
| Wednesday | Upper body strength | Resistance |
| Thursday | Primer + easy cardio | Recovery/NEAT |
| Friday | Full body strength | Resistance |
| Saturday | Cardio (5K build from Phase 2) | Aerobic |
| Sunday | Brisk walk 45–60 min | NEAT |

**Daily steps target:** 10,000–12,000 throughout block.

---

# PHASE 1: FOUNDATION (Weeks 1–4)

**Goals:** Movement quality, machine-based volume, aerobic base, technique audition for barbell work in Phase 2.

| Bird dog | 2 x 8/side | | |

## Session B — Upper Body (Wednesday)

| Pallof press | 2 x 10/side | | |

## Session C — Full Body (Friday)

| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Tempo | Notes |

## Cardio

# Week 12 — 5K Test Protocol

**24–48 hours pre-test:** Reduce strength volume 30%. Normal sleep, food, hydration.

**Test day setup:**
- Chest strap HR monitor — non-negotiable
- Measured course (track, treadmill, or GPS-verified)
- Trainer present
- Water and phone available
- Familiar route — no race environment

**Pacing rules:**
- Start slow — first km should feel easy
- HR cap absolute: hit 115 → walk until HR <105
- Talk test: short sentences possible throughout
- RPE cap 13

**Stop criteria:** Chest pain/pressure, dizziness, disproportionate breathlessness, palpitations, irregular heartbeat awareness, HR fails to drop in walk breaks, anything wrong.

**Post-test:** 10 min walking cool-down minimum. HR <100 within 5 min is good. Record time, average HR, peak HR, RPE, subjective feeling. Photo at finish.

**Framing:** Goal is **completion at controlled intensity**, not maximum effort. Realistic time 35–50 min. The baseline matters more than the number.

# Cueing Non-Negotiables (Barbell Work)

1. Exhale audibly on every rep. Silent rep = rack it.
2. No belt.
3. RIR 3 minimum.
4. No PR attempts — every session is practice.
5. Deadlifts: full reset between reps, fresh breath cycle, no bouncing.
6. Back squat to parallel only, no ATG.
7. Front squat self-limits load — let it.
8. Any dizziness, head pressure, flushing, straining → set ends.
